info.name: Bitculator Data API
info.description: Programmatic access to Bitculator market data: coins, prices, history, exchanges, trust scores, tickers, pairs, wallets, sentiment, technical indicators, liquidations, editorial content, and calculators.

item.name: Coins
item.description:
Ranked coin and token market data: paginated listings, single-coin detail, movers
(gainers/losers), recently-added, trending, and per-coin time series. Prices,
marketcap and supply are decimal STRINGS (floats can't carry market precision);
percentage changes, ranks and counts are numbers.

query.description: How many trending coins to return (1–20, default 10).

request.description:
The most-viewed coins right now, ranked by view `score`. A compact projection
(no pagination): id, slug, name, symbol, rank, price (decimal string), marketcap,
logo and score.

query.description: Content language for the description (falls back to English).

request.description:
Full single-coin profile. Beyond the list fields it adds: `supply`
(circulating/total/max), `today` OHLC, `all_time_high` / `all_time_low` (price,
date and percent_from the current price), `fully_diluted_valuation`, market
`counts` (exchanges/pairs/tickers/wallets), `decimals`, `genesis_date`, official
`links` (typed url list), token `contracts`, and a localized HTML `description`
(falls back to English when the requested locale is missing). All price/supply
fields are decimal strings.

query.description: minutely, half-hourly, hourly or daily (default daily).
ISO date/time lower bound.
ISO date/time upper bound (a date-only value means through that day).
Max rows (1–2000, default 1000).

request.description:
Per-coin OHLC + volume + marketcap time series. Pick `interval`: minutely,
half-hourly, hourly or daily. Retention is a hard property of the rollup
pipeline — minutely 8 days, half-hourly 3 months, hourly 6 months, daily forever;
requests beyond a window return what exists. When a `limit` is set you get the
MOST RECENT N rows in the window, emitted oldest-first. Prices are decimal
strings.

query.description: minutely, half-hourly, hourly or daily (default daily).
ISO date/time lower bound.
ISO date/time upper bound.
Max rows (1–2000, default 1000).

request.description:
The same per-coin rollups as `Candle history`, projected to `{time, marketcap}`
only. Same `interval` choices and retention windows (minutely 8 days,
half-hourly 3 months, hourly 6 months, daily forever), most-recent-N when a
`limit` is set.

query.description: 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, 180d or 365d (default 7d).

request.description:
A compact price series for the coin over the chosen `period`, for drawing
sparklines.

`points` is a sample of at most 480 readings, oldest first, each a decimal-string
`price` at an ISO-8601 `time`. `low` and `high` are the true extremes of the whole
period — they bound every point, but need not appear among the sampled ones.
`change` is the move across the period in PERCENT (`1.25` means +1.25%).

item.name: Prices
item.description:
The lightweight price hot path — current price, marketcap, 24h volume and recent
changes for a requested set of coins. `/prices` requires a selector (ids, slugs or
symbols); `/prices/{slug}` targets one coin. Optionally `convert` into a fiat
currency (crypto prices refresh ~every minute, fiat FX ~twice daily). Prices and
marketcap are decimal strings.

query.description: Coin ids to price (CSV). At least one of ids, slugs or symbols is required; the three lists cap at 100 selectors combined. This field is required when none of slugs and symbols are present. Must not be greater than 1000 characters.
Coin slugs to price (CSV). At least one of ids, slugs or symbols is required. This field is required when none of ids and symbols are present. Must not be greater than 2000 characters.

Coin symbols to price (CSV, case-insensitive). At least one of ids, slugs or symbols is required. This field is required when none of ids and slugs are present. Must not be greater than 1000 characters.
Convert prices/marketcap into an active fiat currency by symbol (default USD). FX rates refresh ~twice daily.

request.description:
Prices for a requested set of coins. Pass at least one selector — `ids`, `slugs`
or `symbols` (up to 100 combined). `meta.currency` echoes the conversion target
(USD unless `convert` is set).

response.body: {"error":{"code":"validation","message":"The request parameters are invalid.","details":{"errors":{"ids":["Pass at least one selector: ids, slugs or symbols."]}}}}

query.description: Active fiat currency symbol to price in (default USD).

request.description:
Single-coin price snapshot. Optionally `convert` into an active fiat currency by
symbol (default USD).

query.description: The coin's slug identifier.
date The lookup date (after 2008-12-31, not in the future).

request.description:
The coin's USD price on a given date, read from the daily history (exact day,
±3-day fallback — the same resolver the portfolio uses). Crypto only: fiat rows
have no daily history.

markets and raw per-exchange trading symbols. All of it is snapshot data — no
per-ticker/pair history exists. USD volumes are numbers; prices are decimal strings.

item.name: Global Market
item.description:
Market-wide aggregates — total marketcap and volume, asset/exchange/pair/market
counts, BTC/ETH dominance with a rank-based top-3, the market Fear & Greed reading,
plus a top-100 heatmap and marketcap/volume history.

request.description:
One-shot market overview: total marketcap and 24h volume, counts of
cryptocurrencies / tokens / exchanges / pairs / markets, `dominance`
(BTC & ETH share plus the rank-based `top3`), and the market `fear_greed`
reading.

Top-100 treemap rows plus framing stats (total marketcap/volume, dominance and
the market Fear & Greed score) — the API twin of the web heatmap.

query.description: 24h, 7d, 30d or all (default 24h).

request.description:
Total-market time series for `marketcap` or `volume`. Granularity follows the
`period`: 24h = half-hourly, 7d = hourly, 30d/all = daily (finer rollups are
pruned).

item.name: Sentiment
item.description:
Market and per-coin sentiment indices. Fear & Greed and Bull/Bear are
15-minute-refresh SNAPSHOTS — only the current reading exists, there is no time
series for them. Altseason carries full daily history. `indicators` is the
market-wide technical tally.

request.description: The coin's bullish/bearish community tallies over the rolling 24h window.

Casts the key owner's sentiment vote for a coin. One vote per key owner per coin
per rolling 24h window — re-voting inside the window updates the existing vote.

query.description: Coin slug for a per-coin reading; omit for the market index.

request.description:
The current Fear & Greed reading (a 15-minute snapshot — no history). Omit `coin`
for the market-wide index, or pass a coin slug for a per-coin reading. `intervals`
carries the 7d/30d sub-scores and their component breakdown.

response.body: {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"No fear & greed data for this scope."}}

query.description: Coin slug for a per-coin reading; omit for the market index.

request.description:
The current Bull/Bear reading (a 15-minute snapshot — no history). Omit `coin`
for the market-wide index, or pass a coin slug for a per-coin reading.

query.description: Days of daily history to include (1–365; 0/omit = current only).

request.description:
The current altseason reading (count of coins beating BTC out of the top 100),
with optional daily `history`. Unlike Fear & Greed, altseason has full daily
history — pass `days` to include it.

The market-wide technical tally — 25 indicator categories rolled up, each with
its current state, score and category data.

item.name: Indicators
item.description:
Per-coin technical indicators. Each indicator is its own dedicated endpoint —
momentum oscillators (RSI, Stoch-RSI, CCI, MFI, Williams %R), trend and price
baselines (SMA, MACD, VWAP), volume flow (OBV, CMF), trend strength (ADX) and
volatility — plus a single multi-indicator snapshot. Every family is a DAILY
series computed from daily candles (full retention; young assets return leading
warm-up `null`s until enough history exists). Price-scale families (SMA, VWAP,
MACD, OBV) emit decimal strings; bounded oscillators emit numbers. A few
long-window periods require a paid plan — noted on each endpoint.

request.description:
The multi-indicator snapshot — every indicator category's latest `state`
(bullish/bearish/sheepish…), `score` and raw `data`, in one payload. Ideal
for a dashboard at-a-glance read; use the dedicated per-indicator endpoints
below for full daily history.

response.body: {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"No indicator data for this coin yet."}}

query.description: Window length — one of 7, 14, 21, 28 (default 14).
ISO date lower bound.
ISO date upper bound.
Max rows (1–1000, default 365).

request.description:

item.name: Alarms
item.description:
Price-alarm CRUD — the same alarms the web app manages. Alarms consume the key
owner's alarm inventory balance, are TARGET-type on coins only, and an above/below
vs current-value guard blocks alarms that would self-trigger instantly. Key-scoped
(the API key sets the owner) and never response-cached.

query.description: Page number (1-based).
Rows per page (1–100, default 25).

request.description:
The key owner's alarms, newest first, paginated. Filter by `status`, `direction`
or `notification` channel.

Creates a TARGET alarm on a coin and spends one alarm slot from the key owner's
balance. The target is checked against the coin's current value so the alarm
cannot self-trigger instantly: an `above` alarm must target more than the current
value, a `below` alarm less.
Deletes one of the key owner's alarms and refunds the alarm slot it consumed.

item.name: Webhooks
item.description:
Bitculator POSTs each event as JSON with an HMAC signature header:

    X-Bitculator-Signature: t=<unix-ts>,v1=<hex hmac_sha256("<ts>.<raw-body>", secret)>
    X-Bitculator-Event: alarm.triggered

Verify it by recomputing the HMAC over "<t>.<raw request body>" with your
endpoint secret and comparing in constant time; reject if `t` is older than a
few minutes (replay guard). Example (PHP):

    [$t, $v1] = sscanf($_SERVER['HTTP_X_BITCULATOR_SIGNATURE'], 't=%d,v1=%s');
    $expected = hash_hmac('sha256', $t.'.'.file_get_contents('php://input'), $secret);
    abort_unless(hash_equals($expected, $v1) && abs(time() - $t) < 300, 403);

Supported events: `alarm.triggered`. Deliveries retry 3× with backoff; an
endpoint auto-disables after 10 consecutive failed deliveries.

request.description:
The key owner's webhook endpoints, newest first. Signing secrets are never
included — each secret is shown exactly once, at creation.

Registers an HTTPS endpoint (max 5 per account) for event deliveries. The
response includes the signing `secret` — the ONLY time it is ever shown, so
store it immediately.

Deletes one of the key owner's webhook endpoints. Pending deliveries to it are
abandoned.

Fires a signed `alarm.triggered` test event (`test: true` in the payload, real
signature headers) so receivers can be verified end-to-end.

Rows per page (1–100, default 25).
